questions.question: What is a key chemical property of the Group 0 elements, also known as the noble gases?
options: They are highly reactive with non-metals.
They are unreactive.
They react violently with water.
They easily form covalent bonds with metals.

questions.question: Which of the following is true about the state of all noble gases at room temperature?
options: They are all gases.
They are all liquids.
They are all solids.
Their states range from gas to solid.

questions.question: Why are noble gases chemically stable and unreactive?
options: They have a high positive charge in their nucleus.
They have complete outer electron shells.
They have very low atomic masses.
They only exist as single diatomic molecules.

questions.question: What trend is observed as you move down Group 0 of the periodic table?
options: Boiling points decrease and they become lighter.
Atomic mass, density and boiling points increase.
Atomic mass decreases while density increases.
They change from gases to solids.

questions.question: How do the properties of elements within each group of the periodic table change as you move down?
options: They change completely randomly.
They stay absolutely identical without any variation.
They change gradually down the group.
They alternate between metallic and non-metallic states.

questions.question: Which of the following describes the properties and trends of Group 1 metals as you go down the group?
options: They become harder and less reactive.
They are soft, have lower densities than most other metals, and become more reactive.
They become denser than transition metals and lose their reactivity.
They change from highly reactive solids to unreactive gases.

questions.question: Why are Group 1 metals referred to as alkali metals?
options: They react with water to form an alkaline solution and hydrogen gas.
They are found naturally in alkaline soils as pure elements.
They form acidic solutions when they react with acids.
They neutralize alkalis to produce salts and water.

questions.question: What products are formed when Group 2 metals react with dilute acids?
options: An alkali and chlorine gas.
A metal oxide and water.
A salt and hydrogen gas.
A salt and oxygen gas.

questions.question: How does the reactivity of Group 2 metals compare to Group 1 metals in the same period?
options: Group 2 metals are more reactive than Group 1 metals.
Group 2 metals are less reactive than Group 1 metals.
Group 2 metals have the exact same reactivity as Group 1 metals.
Group 2 metals are completely unreactive compared to Group 1 metals.

questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic of Group 7 elements?
options: They are all metals with high melting points.
They are all non-metals that have coloured, mostly toxic vapours.
They are unreactive gases with no colour.
They form alkaline solutions when dissolved in water.

questions.question: What trend in the state of matter at room temperature is observed as you go down Group 7?
options: They change from solid to gas.
They change from gas to solid.
They are all liquids.
They remain gases throughout the entire group.

questions.question: How does reactivity change as you move down Group 7 of the periodic table?
options: Reactivity increases.
Reactivity decreases.
Reactivity remains completely unchanged.
The elements become noble and unreactive.

questions.question: What is formed when halogens react with Group 1 and Group 2 metals?
options: Metal hydroxides
Metal carbonates
Metal halides
Metal oxides

questions.question: Which of the following describes a key property of metal halides?
options: They are completely insoluble in water.
They are soluble in water.
They are gaseous at room temperature.
They cannot conduct electricity when dissolved.

questions.question: In the periodic table, what are the vertical columns and horizontal rows called?
options: Columns are called periods, and rows are called groups.
Columns are called groups, and rows are called periods.
Columns are called families, and rows are called categories.
Columns are called series, and rows are called groups.

questions.question: Which Russian scientist is famous for developing the periodic table?
options: Dimitri Mendeleev
Marie Curie
John Dalton
Ernest Rutherford

questions.question: How are elements organized in the periodic table?
options: Alphabetically by their chemical symbols.
Into groups and periods, according to their properties.
Chronologically by the date of their discovery.
Strictly by their state of matter at room temperature.

questions.question: What can be said about elements that belong to the same group in the periodic table?
options: They have completely different, unrelated properties.
They have similar properties.
They always have the same physical state at room temperature.
They have the same atomic mass.

questions.question: Besides being arranged in groups, how else can elements in the periodic table be broadly divided?
options: Into metals (which include transition metals) and non-metals.
Into solids and liquids only.
Into synthetic elements and natural gases only.
Into transition metals and alkali metals only.
